title: HoloFuse: JIT-guided delayed-KV + fused-attn kernel with async continuous batching
author: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Motivation: recent production workloads show that a sizable fraction of token-generation cost is spent in early KV materialization and in repeated rotary/rope transforms applied across micro-batches. This PR introduces a holistic change set that (1) delays KV materialization via a JIT-guided lazy-KV path, (2) introduces a new fused attention microkernel (HoloFuse) that performs FlashAttention-style compute with inlined rotary/rope transforms and fused qkv layout transforms, and (3) wires an async continuous-batching conductor that coalesces requests across short time windows while preserving per-request latency SLOs. The changes are designed to be opt-in via config flags at runtime and are backward compatible with existing model pins.

What this PR does (high level):
- JIT-guided lazy-KV: runtime observes sequence-length distributions and heuristically delays allocating dense KV tensors for short-lived requests; materialization is triggered either by kernel hint or by a thresholded warmup window. This reduces memory churn and eviction pressure on hot caches for open-concurrency workloads.
- HoloFuse kernel: a hand-written CUDA microkernel that combines QKV transpose, rotary/rope application, and the attention softmax/outer-product path in one fused pass; falls back to existing FlashBridge path for unsupported shapes.
- Async continuous batching conductor: a non-blocking scheduling layer that groups in-flight requests into target micro-batches with jittered commit windows. It exposes per-route policy knobs (max-delay-ms, batch-size-target, latency-slo-ms) and integrates with the autoscaler hints.
- Compatibility and safety: feature gated, thorough fallbacks, progressive rollout (canary flag), and telemetry to measure hit-rate of lazy-KV and kernel selection.
commits: feat(lazy-kv): add JIT-guided delayed KV allocation and warmup detector
perf(holo-kernel): add HoloFuse fused-attn CUDA microkernel with rotary inlining
sched(async-batcher): implement continuous-batching conductor and policy knobs
infra: add kernel-selection telemetry counters and rollout feature flag
test: unit+integration tests for lazy-KV and conductor
docs: runtime knobs and canary rollout guide
release_notes:
- Introduces HoloFuse fused-attn kernel (opt-in).
- Adds JIT-guided lazy-KV to reduce memory churn for short-lived requests.
- Adds async continuous-batching conductor with per-route knobs.
- Opt-in by default; enable via runtime.feature_flags.holo_fuse = true
review_thread: Liam Chen (2026-02-19): Please quantify where delayed KV helps vs when it hurts. Can we add metrics to measure lazy-KV hit/miss?
Aisha Kapoor (2026-02-19): Added kernel_selection_metrics and lazy_kv hit-rate counters; expanded tests to include a long-tail trial. Note in docs: default thresholds are conservative.
María Alvarez (2026-02-20): HoloFuse kernel looks good but please ensure FP16 accumulation path preserves numerics; add a comparison test against FlashBridge on known edge cases.
Aisha Kapoor (2026-02-21): Added FP16 accumulation comparison tests and an optional numerics-check mode. Benchmarks attached to PR summary.
Ethan Ross (2026-02-22): Approved. Did an end-to-end canary run on dedicated and hosted clusters; no regressed SLOs observed at 10k qps sustained for 30m.
Priya Nair (2026-02-23): Left a minor nits patch for scheduler config validation; resolved in follow-up commit. Approved.
performance_summary: Microbenchmarks (bert-like 1k batch distribution): p50 token latency reduced by 12-18% depending on seq length; p99 improved by 18-36% on mixed short+long workloads when lazy-KV avoids early materialization. Peak throughput improved up to 1.9x for short-sequence chat workloads on V100/80GB. Memory footprint during high-concurrency scenarios reduced by ~22% at 95th percentile.
testing: Unit tests: attn kernel correctness, FP16 numerics, lazy-KV state transitions. Integration tests: conductor end-to-end with perf harness. CI: unit and perf pipelines passed; perf pipeline re-run twice to stabilize noisy measurements.
rollout_plan: Canary 5% traffic on dedicated capacity for 48h with telemetry gating (error-rate, p99 delta, kernel-fallback-rate). If stable, ramp to 25% for 24h, then 100% opt-in for customers who enable feature flag. Provide immediate rollback by turning off runtime.feature_flags.holo_fuse and draining conductor lanes.
notes: This PR touches low-level kernel code and scheduler; any follow-ups should focus on exposing more fine-grained kernel hints to the compiler and evaluating a dynamic threshold for lazy-KV based on live tail latency signals.
